class_data.name: Martial Arts
class_data.notes:
Your training grants you mastery of unarmed combat and certain weapons. Your Monk weapons are Simple melee weapons and Martial melee weapons with the Light property.

While you are unarmored, not wielding a Shield, and wielding only Monk weapons (or no weapons), you gain the following benefits:
• Bonus Unarmed Strike. You can make one Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.
• Martial Arts Die. You can use a d6 in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons; this die increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the class table.
• Dexterous Attacks. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. When you use your Unarmed Strike to Grapple or Shove, you can use Dexterity instead of Strength to determine the save DC.

class_data.name: Unarmored Defense
class_data.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

class_data.name: Monk’s Focus
class_data.notes:
You gain a pool of Focus Points that fuels certain Monk features. The number of points is shown in the class table. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Some features that use Focus Points require a saving throw; the DC equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

You start knowing the following options:
• Flurry of Blows. You can spend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action.
• Patient Defense. You can take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dodge actions as a Bonus Action.
• Step of the Wind. You can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dash actions as a Bonus Action, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

class_data.name: Unarmored Movement
class_data.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your Speed increases by 10 feet. This bonus increases at higher Monk levels, as shown in the class table.

class_data.name: Uncanny Metabolism
class_data.notes:
When you roll Initiative, you can instantly regain all expended Focus Points. When you do, roll your Martial Arts die and regain Hit Points equal to your Monk level + the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Deflect Attacks
class_data.notes:
When a creature hits you with an attack that deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can use a Reaction to reduce the total damage to you by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can spend 1 Focus Point to redirect the attack. Choose a creature you can see: within 5 feet of you if the original attack was melee, or within 60 feet and not behind Total Cover if it was ranged. That creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier, of the same type as the original attack.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You choose a Monk subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Monk levels.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at levels 8, 12, and 16.

class_data.name: Slow Fall
class_data.notes: When you fall, you can use a Reaction to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

class_data.name: Extra Attack
class_data.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

class_data.name: Stunning Strike
class_data.notes:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can spend 1 Focus Point to attempt to stun it. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.
On a failed save, it is Stunned until the start of your next turn.
On a successful save, its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against it before then has Advantage.

class_data.name: Empowered Strikes
class_data.notes: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, you can choose for the damage to be Force instead of its normal type.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You gain a level 6 feature from your Monk subclass.

subclass_data.name: Shadow Arts
subclass_data.notes:
You draw upon the power of the Shadowfell, gaining the following benefits:

Darkness. Expend 1 Focus Point to cast the Darkness spell without components. You can see within its area. At the start of each of your turns, you may move the area of Darkness to a space within 60 feet.

Darkvision. You gain Darkvision out to 60 feet; if you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

Shadowy Figments. You know the Minor Illusion spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

subclass_data.name: Shadow Step
subclass_data.notes: While entirely in Dim Light or Darkness, you can use a Bonus Action to teleport up to 60 feet to another unoccupied space you can see that is also in Dim Light or Darkness. You then have Advantage on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

effects.name: Giant Ancestry
effects.notes: You are descended from Giants. Choose one of the following benefits—a supernatural boon from your ancestry; you can use the chosen benefit a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest:

effects.name: Large Form
effects.notes: Starting at character level 5, you can change your size to Large as a Bonus Action if you're in a big enough space. This transformation lasts for 10 minutes or until you end it (no action required). For that duration, you have Advantage on Strength checks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

effects.name: Powerful Build
effects.notes: You have Advantage on any ability check you make to end the Grappled condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

effects.name: Cloud's Jaunt
effects.notes: As a Bonus Action, you magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

effects.name: Fire's Burn
effects.notes: When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can also deal 1d10 Fire damage to that target.

effects.name: Frost's Chill
effects.notes: When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can also deal 1d6 Cold damage to that target and reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

effects.name: Hill's Tumble
effects.notes: When you hit a Large or smaller creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can give that target the Prone condition.

effects.name: Stone's Endurance
effects.notes: When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to roll 1d12. Add your Constitution modifier to the number rolled and reduce the damage by that total.

effects.name: Storm's Thunder
effects.notes: When you take damage from a creature within 60 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to deal 1d8 Thunder damage to that creature.

feats.notes: Luck Points. You have a number of Luck Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus and can spend the points on the benefits below. You regain your expended Luck Points when you finish a Long Rest.Advantage. When you roll a d20 for a D20 Test, you can spend 1 Luck Point to give yourself Advantage on the roll.Disadvantage. When a creature rolls a d20 for an attack roll against you, you can spend 1 Luck Point to impose Disadvantage on that roll.
feats.name: Lucky

feats.notes: Enhanced Dual Wielding. When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a weapon that has the Light property, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn with a different weapon, which must be a Melee weapon that lacks the Two-Handed property. You don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative.Quick Draw. You can draw or stow two weapons that lack the Two-Handed property when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.
feats.name: Dual Wielder
